This was a solid scip concept. I think the writeup could be condensed and shortened; many of the details are thoughtful, but ultimately not very engaging. The Series I scips you reference in comments, the ones I remember most vividly, were very short. Strangely enough, your writeup for this SCP strikes me as far more realistic, in that it provides details that a containment specialist would want to review before engaging with the anomaly. My guess is that this realism weakened the piece; after all, most real-life containment procedures would be relatively boring documents.

The brief description of Foundation detective work was good worldbuilding. Unfortunately I think the dry, clinical tone restraint of the SCP format didn't serve that worldbuilding goal; it felt too detailed when I first read it, despite its brevity. After some reflection, I think the problem was actually a lack of space for narrative beats. I'd enjoy reading a tale that depicts the Foundation investigation with a little more vibrancy and drama.

item.title: Re: Carnivorous Tattoo
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there MisterNightmare013. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+crit
-crit

Unfortunately, I’m not sure I completely understand how your scp functions at the moment. So it’s a predatory tattoo that “appears” on random people’s skin? Why wouldn’t the victim automatically be suspicious of its appearance?

Claw mark-like tattoos over existing tattoos/bare skin that seem to sting as would normal claw marks would also appear.

What does this mean? Perhaps you should clarify your wording.

Eventually it would kill its victim in the way the predator its based off would normally kill its prey (bruises associated with being constricted being tattooed on the victim or gashes from claws as well)

Similarly for this statement. How exactly does a victim die? More importantly, why is this happening to victims? How/when does the tattoo appear or choose its victims? There are also sections of your central narrative that jump about and don’t make sense, mainly:

- why would the Foundation investigate a random string of murders? What made them anomalous to begin with?
- why is the Foundation agent sensing a stinging sensation?
- “the form of extinct species of Kaprosuchu” what’s the relevance of this?
- “the Agent willingly accepted being contained and observed to determine the entities behavior.” I’d think the Foundation would conduct more than just observations if they discovered the entity was a tattoo.
- “Its main way of hunting would appear to try and make its prey paranoid all the while it toys with its prey.” I still don’t understand how this would work. Perhaps you could give a specific, detail example.

The concept itself sounds cool, but I have a feeling you have not fleshed out the exact mechanics of your proposed scip. As a result, its anomalous properties sound random / too fantastical and as a result, I can’t really imagine the scp as realistically working.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. Best of luck!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Carnivorous Tattoo

The line about the trash cans not containing any bones was perfectly placed and camouflaged. My headcanon is that the Foundation is focused on investigating the wrong thing here, and some other entity is pleased with the success of its obfuscation. Is this scip actually contained? We'll never know for sure, but I love how clear it is that something more than "weirdly localized definition of a word" could be going on here. The dadaist-meme funniness of the word "boneless" takes the edge off of what could have been just as thoroughly creepy as the scip that used to be a library, but that's okay; the world don't need two antimemetic scips with that precise line of emphasis.

Forum thread: SCP-3181

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Undercover Fly. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I see that you’ve revised the article a few times based on the other reviewers’ feedback. Unfortunately, my concerns boil down to two that I hope you can expand on / clarify:

1) Plot inconsistencies / lack of clarity. Why is this happening? It’s never hinted at / explained in your pitch besides mention of the Chaos Insurgency. More importantly, why is the majority of objects at the center “human corpses”, and how is it possible that they number in the billions? Just what exactly is happening? Why are the agents “blind, deaf and mute”? If so, how do they even use a computer? Similarly, why does the effect suddenly wear off and they die? Lastly, the Foundation not pursuing containment of the anomaly is not in line with their motto.

2) There still isn’t a coherent / developed narrative. The only line I can glimpse from your Central Narrative portion is an exploration log? Basically, the MTF goes incorporeal, communicate with the Foundation, and then they die? You need more than that, especially if you want to give your readers some semblance of answers as to what’s going on. Other suggestions might be to explain the origins of the anomaly, how/why the CI is involved and how exactly the Foundation goes about trying to contain this.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. Best of luck!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth

I don't think this is a "Safe" SCP by current standards. Arguably it's Keter, because, as the author says above,

Rabbits can migrate, you miss one or two and they breed like, well, rabbits, so in a few years you've got the same problem again; dealing with this requires a large scale effort (you've got to comb every inch of half of Georgia), and the Foundation finds it easier to amnesticize ~20 people per year affected by this.

If the Foundation can't feasibly contain an anomaly, and constant vigilance and regular follow-up action is required in order to address instances' effects after-the-fact, that's Keter, right? I'm still learning, so I'm open to hearing explanations to the contrary.

item.title: Re: The Humanoids
item.content:encoded:
Hello GodlyUser! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious software appears along with a mysterious PC out of nowhere and seems to grant mindless beings knowledge to act as sapient beings. However, they can't recall their past nor origin and seem to have only a small piece of their memories.

This feels a bit close to a "thing that does a thing", the anomaly isn't explained or given any clear purpose/motive, which both makes the skip feel like a random object and makes it harder for me as the reader to become invested in the concept. What is the skips in-universe reason for existing? why does it function this way? how/why can't affected individuals remember anything about their past?

::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
Currently there isn't any clear central narrative, as this only comes across as additional info. What is the setup, middle act, payoff and conflict? what happens in the narrative? who are the characters? how will the story make me feel? whats everything building up to? how will all of the below info fit into a draft/narrative?

I would highly recommend you start development on a clear narrative, modern audiences tend to favour narratives which has lead to them more or less becoming the standard.

The narrative:

This software was discovered when one of the Foundation personnel noticed strange sounds from one of the enhanced containment chambers that're containing non-sapient SCPs. They discovered that it is talking and chatting on a PC that shows up out of nowhere.

This could work as a setup, however there isn't anything expanding on where the skip came from or why it might be here. Just having the skip show up out of nowhere with no context, comes off as a quick way to get out of developing the skip fully. Along with this, The Foundation doesn't seem to look into its appearance, which feels a bit out of character for them, considering this could be seen a containment hazard at the very least.

This SCP originally is a PC that appears to have an unknown chatroom with unidentified programmers. This chatroom's software is named "The Humanoids," seemingly designed for both sapient and non-sapient anomalies to interact with each other through the technology screens. Any non-sapient/mindless humanoid entities/beings who come in contact with the screen will eventually be granted the knowledge to act as beings that aren't mindless. They can also interact with others as long as the PC isn't shut down. Of course, they may also embody human nature and act like regular humans, and some act very smart.

Who are these programmers? what role do they play in concept and narrative? why do they cause non-sentient beings to become sapient? are these effects permanent?- Currently there isn't much context to the programmers or what they actually do, as a result they feel disconnected from the rest of the concept.

However, despite being granted sapient knowledge, the humanoid entities cannot remember their origins, and some seem only to recall a small piece of their memories.

There isn't anything expanding on or explaining this.- how does this relate back to the skip itself? why does it happen?

Attempted to delete the software or destroy the PC is proven to be impossible, for it is shown to be constructed out of mysterious unidentified materials and seemingly has a powerful firewall to prevent hackers from infiltrating into it.

The use of "mysterious materials", feels like a quick way to keep audience attention and/or make the skip more interesting, while also getting out of further developing the skip. Currently this feels a bit OP, which makes it hard for me stay interested the idea.

However, the Foundation didn't try their best efforts in an attempt to erase the software nor wreck the PC, for it is because, with the help of "The Humanoids" chatroom, the hostile non-sapient SCPs appear to have good behaviors rather than being hostile, evil, and aggressive. However, the chatroom doesn't actually change the behaviors of sapient SCPs as they still have their original personalities.

Why would they try to destroy it in the first place? even if the software or PC was actively dangerous, they would contain it first and foremost.- why would they try to destroy something that they know nothing about to begin with, it sounds unnecessarily risky.

Along with this, Their willingness to test this on other SCPs feels odd to me. The Foundation would be much more likely to test this on animals first, before making any decisions on cross testing.

Which brings me to another issue; why does the skip change other SCPs behaviour? currently, this effect makes the skip feel like a device that just magically pacifies any SCP with no context.- this aspect seems to come out of nowhere, and it takes focus off the original idea and puts on other SCPs, as its effects are now entirely based around other articles.

Do note that cross testing in general is risky, considering the outcomes can vary greatly and there is no guarantee that it wouldn't cause a disaster. Considering the PC doesn't change personality, if something malevolent was given sapience, then a whole range of new issues could arise. -To sum up, using this on other skips feels way too risky, considering how much could go wrong.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Overall, the skip currently feels a a bit close to a "thing that does a thing", mainly due to the lack of a clear purpose and the lack of a strong narrative. Some of the effects feel a bit unrelated to one another, along with a some taking focus away from the skip entirely.

In general, I would recommend getting a clearer idea of what the skip actually is, expand further upon what the programmers are, what they do, and why they do it. Try to cut any unnecessary or confusing details/anomalies, as it can confuse the main focus.- I would also recommend you avoid relying on cross testing as it takes focus away from your skip.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hey there! I go by "DrStinkyBacteriaV2" in tribute to my previous wikidot account "DrStinkyBacteria" which I have not accessed in over 2 years now. I've been into the SCP genre for over 3 years now and I have finally taken it upon myself to begin fantasizing on several ideas I have loathed over. But, I'm truly getting ahead of myself.

The real reason I finally decide to revive my previous wikidot account is because, well, I had written an entire SCP on the SCP Wiki Sandbox and never did anything with it; how foolish of me to allow such fantastic ideas go to waste, right? Anyways the ideas had some merit to them and I thought I'd revive them along with a set goal to have a long-standing within this genre.

But anyways, I currently have nothing better to do with my life, especially consider that it is Christmas Break for me at the moment, and Covid is giving me quite a bit of free time to say the least. I am quite frankly excited to get to encounter new people and I am also looking forward to endlessly typing on this site. Right now living in a tiny as hell duplex In-the-Middle-of-Nowhere, Tennessee and I'd say that I am having the time of my life, with my introverted self, at this computer.

Sorry for any grammar mistakes this may have, I have been up all night and I am writing this now at 3:35 AM.

item.title: You're It (SCP concept)
item.content:encoded:
An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction to survivors of the attacks. Those affected by this SCP will cease to be afflicted after passing it on.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

This SCP is a phenomenon that causes afflicted individuals to quickly become more hostile and violent towards others, as well as giving them increased physical strength and resistance to injury. The exact cause of this is unknown, as no pathogen or other potential source has yet to be identified. This SCP will likely cause affected individuals to attack nearby people, often resulting in their deaths. Those who survive these attacks will begin to exhibit the same anomalous effects as their attacker, while the attacker will slowly lose the aggression and increased strength.

Those that have "passed on" the SCP have a moderate chance to die of multiple organ failure after the effects have subsided, and those that live retain memories of their actions while under the influence of this SCP. Should the current carrier of this SCP die before passing it on, it will instead be passed on to the carrier's killer. If the carrier was not killed by a sapient being, the SCP will instead pass on to a random individual, where nearer individuals are more likely to be afflicted.

This SCP is contained via an afflicted D-Class personnel inside a reinforced concrete humanoid containment chamber. The D-Class is kept alive as long as possible, and their vitals are constantly monitored. Additional D-Class personnel are introduced into the chamber to allow the SCP to be passed on. The previous carrier will be tranquilized via remotely controlled sentries before they can kill the new carrier. The previous carrier, now sedated, is removed from the chamber and amnestics are administered.

item.title: Do you know what lies outside the edge of the horizon?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): mystery/cosmic

Elevator Pitch: I had just died, but the how and why of my passing is not a subject of importance, for the information I shall make aware next is the highest of priority to all living beings.

Central Narrative: a man dies and his soul is transported outside the edge of the visible universe/big bang's horizon and meets inexistence itself. In the end, he too becomes inexistence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: at the end, it is revealed that this whole tale was a message somehow sent to his daughter to say goodbye and tell her that the last thought he had was of her.

Additional Notes: Any idea to make it more interesting I guess
